craft_notes: Same work voice (quatrain, dash breaths); new song, new sthāyin: ānanda as everything-is-already-yoga — bhakti in the mode of pratyabhijñā (recognition), vyabhicāri harṣa (joy that all utterance/posture/breath is already mantra/mudrā/yoga). Verse color: recognition over technique; nothing enjoined, everything shining. Firing rows: the source's own engine is threefold repetition-with-variation (yat…saḥ / yat…sā / yat…saḥ, row 9) → English anaphora, capital 'Whatever' line-initial ×3; verb-final bhrājate (row 1) → end-weight 'shine' line-final and song-final; close is interrogative kim…na bhrājate (L0 p027) → the question IS the close again (v2's principle holds: the question is the period), but here it affirms — 'what would NOT shine?' means everything shines, so the vowel arc runs bright-to-brightest, the inverse of v2's dark settle. First-person mama (L0 p026) kept as 'I' per row 11 deixis: the Sanskrit particularizes, so English particularizes — generalizing to 'one' would betray the trace. FULL-LAYER AUDIT: L0 no forks (all fork:none); three redefinitions map cleanly p000–p007 (sound→mantra), p008–p014 (posture→mudrā), p015–p022 (breath-flow→yoga); śākta kept transliterated per L3 note (abode-of-Śakti vs of-the-śākta open — do not resolve in song). NOTE confirms 'Nothing enjoined; utterance, posture, breathing are recognized as already mantra, mudrā, yoga' + 'shining is the default' — the draft's arc is the analysis sung. REJECTED OPTIONS (with killers): (a) L3 couplet kept as 2 long lines → killed by work voice (v1/v2 quatrain) + row 9: anaphora needs line-initial repetition to scan, three redefinitions need three breaths. (b) lowercase mid-line 'whatever' → killed by the device itself: unstressed repetition isn't anaphora. (c) 'transcendent' for lokottara (L0 gloss) → killed by rule 15 + singability: L3's 'beyond the world' is frozen and breathes; both trace p007. (d) dropping line-4 'and' → killed by small-edits rule: L3's joint, keep it. (e) 'while I experience' (L2) over L3's 'as I experience it' → killed by L3-frozen; both trace p026. (f) declarative close ('everything shines.') → killed by kim interrogative + v2 precedent: stating what the verse asks drops the rank. Read aloud: three gathering Whatever-lines, one bright closing question — the breath opens, not stops.

lines: Whatever sound rises from the mouth — that mantra is beyond the world;
whatever stance this pleasure-pain-born body takes — that itself is mudrā;
whatever flowing of breath in its own rhythm — that itself is wondrous yoga;
and the supreme śākta abode — as I experience it, what would not shine?
notes: śākta kept transliterated per L3 (of-Śakti vs of-the-śākta open)
l4.sanskrit_cite: śabdaḥ kaścana yo mukhādudayate mantraḥ sa lokottaraḥ saṃsthānaṃ sukhaduḥkhajanmavapuṣo yatkāpi mudraiva sā | prāṇasya svarasena yatpravahaṇaṃ yogaḥ sa evādbhutaḥ śāktaṃ dhāma paraṃ mamānubhavataḥ kinnāma na bhrājate
